## Build plan

**1. Header**  
A slim horizontal bar: Tidepool wordmark on the left, “How it works,” “For teams,” and “Pricing” centered, “Get started” as a button on the right. Use warm white, ink-blue text, and a small sea-glass accent in the logo. Set navigation in a crisp sans serif; keep it quiet and easy to scan.

**2. Hero**  
Use a two-column layout: concise pitch and paired calls to action on the left, a large product-window mockup on the right. Show a shared weekly board with tasks, owners, and a few open questions—not a phone collage. Background: pale sand, with soft aqua panels and a restrained tangerine highlight. Headline: **“Make a week your whole team can get behind.”** Support with one sentence about planning together, seeing what matters, and adjusting as work changes. Buttons: “Try Tidepool” and “See how it works.”

**3. Product proof**  
Place a full-width, framed dashboard image below the hero, with three small labels pointing to real interface details: priorities, owners, and flexible plans. Use thin ink-blue rules and simple line icons. Caption: **“One shared plan. Fewer surprises.”**

**4. How it works**  
Three equal cards in a row: **Gather the week**, **Agree on priorities**, **Adapt together**. Each gets a short explanation and a small, distinct illustration—sticky-note shapes, a priority marker, and a plan being rearranged. Keep illustrations geometric and airy; avoid faux hand-drawn annotations.

**5. Team benefits**  
A split section pairs a short, practical copy block with a cropped product view showing comments and ownership. Use a deep blue background with white type and a sea-glass panel. Copy focuses on fewer status-chasing messages and clear next steps, without promising perfect productivity.

**6. Customer voice**  
Use a large sans-serif testimonial in a clean white card, with customer name, role, and team size beneath it. Keep the quote conversational and specific: a team describing how Monday planning now feels clearer.

**7. Closing CTA and footer**  
Finish with a centered headline—**“Give your team a better start to the week.”**—and one prominent “Get started” button. Footer includes product, company, and help links. Across the page, use generous spacing, accessible contrast, and sea-glass, ink blue, warm white, and sparing tangerine.

## Revised build plan

**1. Header**  
A compact horizontal header with Tidepool’s wordmark, links to “How it works” and “For teams,” and a high-contrast “Get started” button. Use warm white, deep navy, and a small sea-glass mark. Set the wordmark in a sturdy sans serif; keep navigation understated.

**2. Hero**  
Two-column layout: the left side carries the pitch and calls to action; the right side shows a crisp, realistic view of a shared team plan. The mockup should show a weekly agenda with priorities, owners, and one changed plan—not a day-by-day timeline or shopping-list-like checklist. Use a pale sand background, navy text, sea-glass surfaces, and a small tangerine accent.  
**Headline:** “A clearer plan for the week, made together.”  
**Supporting copy:** “Bring priorities, owners, and changes into one shared view—so everyone knows what matters next.”  
Buttons: **“Start planning”** and “See how it works.”

**3. The shared plan, up close**  
Show a wide product screenshot with three restrained callouts: **“Set priorities,” “Make ownership clear,”** and **“Adjust when plans change.”** Use fine leader lines, not sketchy annotations. Caption: **“The plan stays useful as the week shifts.”**

**4. How Tidepool works**  
Three numbered cards in a single row: **1. Gather the work. 2. Agree on what matters. 3. Keep the plan current.** Pair each with a simple geometric illustration—overlapping notes, a highlighted priority, and a rearranged calendar block. Add one concise explanatory sentence per step.

**5. Benefits for the team**  
Use a navy panel with a product crop on one side and short copy on the other. Emphasize practical outcomes: fewer “who’s doing this?” messages, clearer handoffs, and shared context when priorities change. Keep claims grounded and specific.

**6. Customer proof**  
Place an approved customer quote in a bright, spacious card, set in the same readable sans serif as the body copy. Include the person’s name, role, and team; use a real quote rather than inventing a testimonial.

**7. Closing CTA and footer**  
End on warm white with **“Start next week with a plan everyone can see.”** and a prominent **“Get started”** button. Finish with compact product, company, and help links.
